_notes.model_currency: USD — TSMC prices wafers and guides in USD; TWD value = USD value x spot FX
_notes.base_year: FY2026E revenue US$176,120m = 1Q26 35.90 + 2Q26 40.20 + 3Q26 46.72 (6-K) + 4Q26 guidance midpoint 53.30; +43.9% vs FY2025 US$122,420m (4Q25 Management Report)
_notes.net_debt: TSMC-reported 3Q26 net cash NT$2,985.40bn (cash & marketable securities 4,016.98 less total interest-bearing debt 1,031.58) less customer temporary receipts NT$234.23bn and lease liabilities NT$36.88bn (both 30-Jun-26, latest disclosed) = NT$2,714.29bn; NCI NT$45.33bn; at 32.478
_notes.wacc: USD cost of equity 10.58% = US 10Y 4.94% (US Treasury par curve, 2026-10-30) + beta 1.24 (TSM 5Y monthly; benchmark not printed by Yahoo/StockAnalysis, presumed S&P 500) x ERP 4.55%. ERP: Damodaran's implied US ERP of 4.20% (2026-10-01) was solved against a 5.29% T-bond, i.e. an implied market return of 9.49%; held constant at the 10-30 yield of 4.94% that is an ERP of 4.55% (conservative: the market fell in October, which raises the implied return). Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Country risk is in the hazard overlay, not the discount rate.
_notes.hazard: 1.5%/yr probability of a cross-strait event destroying 80% of operating value (14% over 10 years)
_notes.capex_da: D&A/revenue 15.5% (2027) rising to 23% (FY2015-24 average ~24%); capex/revenue 34% fading to 28% in Base and Bear (Bull +2-3pp in 2028-31: growth costs capex; Bear 36% in 2028 as capex is sticky on falling revenue). Terminal Base reinvestment = capex 28% - D&A 23% + dNWC ~0.2% = 5.2% of revenue, i.e. ~14% of NOPAT, implying RONIC ~ g / reinvestment rate ~ 22%. Terminal capex is below TSMC's FY15-25 minimum (30.5%) because terminal growth is 3-4%, not the 16.5% CAGR of FY15-25.
_notes.sbc: 0 — TSMC employee compensation is cash profit-sharing already in COGS/opex; restricted stock awards immaterial
_notes.roll_forward: 12-month TP = fair value x (1 + USD cost of equity) at spot FX - NT$24 dividends (4 x NT$6.00; 3Q26 dividends paid NT$155.59bn / 25,932m shares). No FX forecast: the interest-parity alternative would build in ~2.8% TWD appreciation.
_notes.margins: Margins are driven as EBITDA (cash) margin; EBIT = EBITDA - D&A. FY2015-25 EBITDA margin (OPM + D&A/revenue) mean 66.3%, SD 2.4pp, max 68.9% (FY2025); 3Q26 73.4%, 2026E 74.2%. Bull holds 74%; Base returns to the FY2025 record of 68.9% by 2030; Bear troughs at 61% in 2028 (FY2019: 61.6%) and settles at 64.5%.
_notes.other_adjustments: Plus 3Q26 long-term investments NT$224.63bn at book (associates and other investments), US$6916 m.
_notes.scenarios: Bull: 2027 +37% (consensus FY27 revenue NT$7.68T, +37.6%, StockAnalysis 40 analysts 2026-10-16), 2028 +27% (Goldman Sachs +28%), 18% fading to 4%; cash margin held at 74%. Base: 2027 +32% (4Q26 guided run-rate plus ~3.5% a quarter; Goldman +32%), 2028 +18% (hyperscaler capex growth forecasts for 2028: +5% Allianz, +6% UBS, +7% DoubleLine, +12% Goldman), 12% fading to 4%; EBITDA margin back to the FY2025 record 68.9% by 2030. Bear (20%): 2023-style correction in 2028 (-10%; FY2023 -8.7%), EBITDA trough 63% (FY2019 61.6%, FY2023 67.2%), settling at 65%. Bust (5%): 2001-style revenue fall in 2028 (-25%; FY2001 -24.3%), EBITDA trough 52%, settling at 63%.
